claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children.

Let me start by asking: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh hello! Yes, I'm looking into claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child named Alex.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about your circumstances. **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Before I can assess eligibility, let me first check the detailed rules. Let me gather the specific criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I can see that the eligibility rules state that you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. However, for children 16 and over, you can normally still qualify if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 18, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in any approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more question to be thorough: **Is Alex currently working? If so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me also check the other guidance to ensure I have the complete picture.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

**However, I need to clarify one important detail before I give my final decision:** You mentioned you have one child named Alex who is 18 years old, not in approved education or training, and not working. 

For my final assessment, I need to confirm: **Does Alex currently live with you, and are you responsible for him (for example, are you providing financial support for his food, clothes, accommodation, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to provide my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16
- For children aged 16 and over, you can only continue to claim if they are under 20 **and** in approved education or training
- Alex is 18 and is not currently in any approved education or training, so he does not meet the eligibility criteria

If Alex were to enter approved education or training in the future (such as university, college, or a recognised training programme), you would be able to claim Child Benefit again, provided he is still under 20.

If you have any questions or if circumstances change, you can contact HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for further advice.
